A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HR-Align research. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. All pages were inspected; v3 adds an appendix, while v2 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original Adroit, RLBench and real-world manipulation experiments, including success rates in Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds ablation and controlled-comparison results in Tables S1–S3.

M1.justification: The HR-Align adapters, language-guided feature aggregation and contrastive alignment objective remain unchanged. The appendix documents existing downstream implementations and tests variants without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RH20T subset, two Adroit tasks, 18 RLBench tasks and five real-world tasks. The appendix controls reuse existing human and robot videos, and its illustrations depict retained tasks.

E2.justification: The main comparator sets remain unchanged. Appendix S3 adds evaluated adapter-based variants, R3M-PreTA and R3M-ClSA, alongside the existing R3M-PreT and R3M-ClS objectives.

E3.justification: Appendix S3 adds comparisons training baselines on both human and robot videos, then matching HR-Align's trainable parameter count. These supplement v2's robot-only, full-parameter comparisons. The original evaluation budgets and metrics remain unchanged; newly specified viewpoints and implementation choices are disclosures.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained adapter-placement ablation and t-SNE analysis, v3 adds a language-guidance ablation and controls for training-data amount and trainable parameters in Tables S1–S3. This substantially broadens the analysis of component contributions and alternative explanations for HR-Align's advantage.

E5.justification: Adroit's three-seed averaging and RLBench's three-test mean and standard-deviation reporting are retained. The appendix adds point estimates without introducing new run-count information, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 and Figure 3 retain their scores. Table S1 adds an average of 80.0 without language guidance versus 81.3 with it. Tables S2–S3 add 78.1/77.5 for full-data R3M-PreT/R3M-ClS and 77.2/76.9 for their adapter variants, compared with HR-Align's 81.3. These are additional conditions, not revisions of the original scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(6) remain equivalent. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs or derivations appear in the appendix.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same adaptation-paradigm contribution, semantic-alignment claim, generalization scope and reported success-rate improvement claims. The appendix supplies additional support without redefining those central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix S3 interprets language-guided feature enhancement as helping semantic alignment and explicitly addresses fairness through matched data and parameter comparisons. The existing interpretations of adapter placement and feature clustering, and the limitations in Section 5, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices S1–S2 substantially expand reproduction details: RLBench encoder replacement and removal of spatial downsampling, real-world camera placement, demonstration recording, recorded state fields, image resolutions and the ACT implementation source. v3 also specifies Adroit's top view and adds a project link. It removes the dataset-configuration release promise and approximate one-fifteenth training-cost comparison; actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds computer-vision and grasping references, and Figure S1 adds attribution to Ma et al. The CLIP reference is removed. These are limited background changes; positioning against proxy-task training and downstream fine-tuning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely preserved. v3 adds appendix subsections, cross-references and acknowledgements, makes localized setup and related-work edits, and updates affiliations and contact information.

P2.justification: v3 adds supplementary Tables S1–S3, an RLBench task gallery in Figure S1 and real-world demonstration sequences in Figure S2. Existing figures and tables retain their designs, with local resizing and repositioning, particularly Figure 4.

improvement.justification: The appendix addresses a weakness in v2's Table 3 through data- and parameter-matched comparisons, adds evidence for language guidance, and makes the evaluation implementations more reproducible. These provide a useful, localized strengthening of the existing paper. The main findings remain unchanged, and the new comparison tables provide no additional uncertainty reporting.
